data.q: In ASP.NET Core, which method is used to configure the HTTP request pipeline?
data.e: The Configure method in the Startup class (or Program.cs in minimal APIs) is where middleware components are added to the request pipeline.

data.q: Where are services registered for Dependency Injection in ASP.NET Core?
data.e: The ConfigureServices method (or WebApplicationBuilder.Services in .NET 6+) is used to register services with the built-in DI container.

data.q: What is the default configuration file name in ASP.NET Core?
data.e: ASP.NET Core uses appsettings.json by default for configuration settings. web.config is used for IIS integration only.

data.q: Which middleware component serves static files (CSS, JS, images) from the wwwroot folder?
data.e: UseStaticFiles() enables serving static files. UseDefaultFiles() serves default documents (index.html). UseFileServer() combines both.

data.q: In .NET 6+, what replaces the separate Program.cs and Startup.cs files?
data.e: .NET 6 introduced top-level statements, allowing the entry point and service/pipeline configuration to reside in a single Program.cs file.

data.q: Which interface represents a component that processes HTTP requests in the middleware pipeline?
data.e: IMiddleware defines a middleware component with an InvokeAsync method. It supports per-request activation via DI.

data.q: What is the purpose of the 'UseRouting' middleware?
o: To match incoming requests to endpoints
data.e: UseRouting adds route matching to the pipeline. It selects an endpoint based on the request URL. UseEndpoints executes the selected endpoint.

data.q: Which attribute designates a class as a Controller in ASP.NET Core MVC?
data.e: [Controller] marks a class as a controller. [ApiController] adds API-specific behaviors. [Route] defines routing templates.

data.q: How do you access a configuration value (e.g., 'ConnectionStrings:Default') in a controller?
data.e: IConfiguration supports both the indexer syntax and the GetConnectionString extension method for connection strings.

data.q: What is the lifetime of a service registered with 'AddScoped'?
o: A new instance for every request
A single instance for the application lifetime
A new instance every time it is requested
A new instance per user session
data.e: Scoped services are created once per client request (connection). Singleton is application-wide. Transient is every time requested.

data.q: Which method enables Razor Pages in an ASP.NET Core application?
data.e: AddRazorPages() adds services for Razor Pages. AddControllersWithViews() is for MVC. AddRazorComponents() is for Blazor.

data.q: What does the [ApiController] attribute automatically handle?
data.e: [ApiController] enables automatic HTTP 400 responses for validation errors, binding source inference, and problem details for errors.

data.q: Which launchSettings.json profile is used when running 'dotnet run'?
o: The profile named after the project
The first profile in the file
data.e: By default, 'dotnet run' uses the profile matching the project name (the 'project' profile), which runs Kestrel directly.

data.q: How do you define a route parameter constraint (e.g., integer ID) in attribute routing?
data.e: Constraints like :int, :guid, :bool, :regex are added after the parameter name separated by a colon.

data.q: What is the purpose of 'UseHttpsRedirection' middleware?
o: Enforces HTTPS by redirecting HTTP requests
data.e: It redirects HTTP requests to HTTPS. It is typically used with UseHsts for production security.

data.q: Which class provides access to the current HTTP request/response in a service or middleware?
data.e: IHttpContextAccessor (registered via AddHttpContextAccessor) allows injecting HttpContext into services. HttpContext itself is scoped to the request.

data.q: What is 'Minimal APIs' in ASP.NET Core?
o: A lightweight framework for building HTTP APIs with less boilerplate
data.e: Introduced in .NET 6, Minimal APIs allow defining endpoints directly in Program.cs using lambda expressions, reducing ceremony compared to Controllers.
